rationale: ROUND 3 of bugs_open/264. Round 2 (50ee4b26) returned REVISE, gated by prior_art_librarian on ONE high-severity point: round 2's rebuttal to the duplicate-active-row objection (active_rows=1 for all four auditor types) never checked it against the STANDING LANDMINE that names 'four agent types' with duplicate active rows, and the count-4 coincidence was left unreconciled. That is now settled directly: the landmine names its four types explicitly (chief-strategist, content-creator, content-creator-contact, site-component-architect — measured 2026-08-09), and none of them is one of this bug's four auditors. Re-running the landmine's OWN exact check live, right now, confirms it: exactly those same four types (and no others, including none of the audit four) currently have duplicate active rows fleet-wide. prior_art_librarian's secondary medium point (brief-fidelity-auditor's 'zero callers' claim rests on tables outside the council's queryable schema) is acknowledged as a genuine scope limit of the council's own checking ability, not a defect in the claim — restated honestly as independently verified outside this gate, not council-reverifiable. debug_historian's medium point (hand-apply-then-record-only for migration 399 could have collided with another session claiming the same number) is checked directly: no collision exists (one file on disk, one matching ledger row). editquality's medium point (the ROLLBACK file is a no-op restatement and should not be counted as a plan edit) is applied: it is removed from edits and folded into grounded_in. Nothing in the actual fix has changed since round 1 — this round is entirely the last piece of verification evidence.

grounded_in: SETTLES prior_art_librarian's round-2 GATING objection (high): the standing landmine (docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/LANDMINES.md, 'Four agent types have TWO active definition rows...') names its four types EXPLICITLY, measured 2026-08-09: chief-strategist, content-creator, content-creator-contact, site-component-architect. None of these is brief-fidelity-auditor, content-quality-auditor, site-review-agent, or visual-design-auditor — the count-4 coincidence the reviewer flagged is exactly that, a coincidence, not the same instance.

Re-running the landmine's OWN exact check (not a paraphrase) live 2026-08-14, fleet-wide, no restriction to the four auditor types: SELECT type, count(*) FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1 → returns EXACTLY chief-strategist=2, content-creator=2, content-creator-contact=2, site-component-architect=2, and NO OTHER type, including none of the four auditors. This is the landmine's authoritative check, not round 1's narrower per-type query, and it independently confirms the same conclusion: zero overlap between the landmine's population and this bug's four.

ACKNOWLEDGES prior_art_librarian's round-2 medium point honestly rather than re-arguing it: the brief-fidelity-auditor 'zero live callers' finding rests on scheduled_tasks and orchestration_states, which this council's own schema access cannot query — so it is independently verified outside the gate (direct psql, both queries quoted in bugs_open/264 §13), not council-reverifiable, and should be read with that caveat rather than as gate-checked fact. This does not change the finding, which is stated as a disclosed pre-existing gap, not load-bearing for whether THIS plan's fix is safe to ship.

SETTLES debug_historian's round-2 medium objection (hand-apply-then-record collision risk): ls docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/399* lists exactly two files (the migration and its ROLLBACK sidecar) — no competing 399-numbered file was ever created by another session. SELECT filename, applied_at, applied_by FROM schema_migrations WHERE filename LIKE '399%' returns exactly one row, applied_by='record-only', filename matching this migration's name byte-for-byte. No collision occurred.

RESPONDS to debug_historian's round-2 low point (no formal idempotency guard): the UPDATE statements are jsonb_set on fixed literal target values, not an increment or an append — replaying the same file twice sets the same keys to the same values both times, so a second run is a no-op in EFFECT even without an explicit pre-state-marker skip. Not upgraded to a formal guard this round (would require editing an already-recorded, already-applied migration file, which this shop's own migration convention forbids — 'fix it, or supersede it with the next number, rather than editing an already-recorded file'); accepted as a low-severity, non-blocking note for any future migration of this shape.

APPLIES editquality's round-2 medium note: the ROLLBACK file, which changes nothing and was correctly identified as a no-op restatement, is removed from this round's edit list (was edit 4 in round 2) and is folded into this grounded_in entry instead: docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/399_four_auditors_audit_source_resolves_to_a_real_value_ROLLBACK.sql exists, is unchanged since round 1, and restores the pre-migration audit_source literals and step wiring, guarded by its own DO block.

Round 1 and round 2's other settled points carry forward unchanged and are not re-argued here: git-grounded fallback removal (3621ca7cf~1), full unfiltered write_audit_findings caller inventory (exactly the same four, no fifth, any status), owning-pipeline naming (improvement-loop→site-review-agent→content-quality-auditor; design-audit-agent→visual-design-auditor and →content-quality-auditor), snapshot_agent() pre-image backups (house convention, already in the applied file), and the new unit test (29ae07500).
